To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) neutrino oscillations between the ordinary and the mirror world can suppress the observed neutrino fluxes at IceCube, (b) this suppression is flavour dependent and (c) the suppression is energy independent.

the non-observation at IceCube can be explained by neutrino oscillation in a model with pseudo-Dirac neutrino and a mirror world, and the predicted flavour ratio at IceCube is significantly different than the standard prediction of 1:1: 1.

we propose a model that can explain the non-observation at IceCube of muon neutrinos from GRBs in terms of a pseudo-Dirac neutrino scenario with a tiny mass splitting between the ordinary and mirror worlds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a possible particle physics origin of the IceCube observations.

the question of how to explain the IceCube observation of the non- observation of the expected muon neutrino event rate in the context of a model that can explain the observed flavour ratios of neutrinos in the cosmic rays and the non observation of the expected number of events at IceCube in the context of an underlying model that can explain both these observations simultaneously.
a possible explanation of the Icecube observation of the suppression of the muon neutrinos in the context of neutrino physics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
if IceCube observations are confirmed in the future, it will be a strong indication of a mirror world and pseudo-Dirac neutrino masses.

the non-observation by IceCube can be explained by a model of pseudo-Dirac neutrino masses and a mirror world, with mass splitting of the order of 10^−15 eV^2, and a difference of the flavour ratios of 1:1.5:2.
a pseudo-Dirac neutrino scenario, with a mass splitting of order 10^(-16) eV^({2}) and an interaction with a mirror world, can explain the non-observation at IceCube of muon neutrinos from GRBs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have proposed an explanation of the Ice-Cube observation that the mu-neutrino flux is lower compared to the standard expectation, in terms of pseudo-Dirac neutrino oscillations in the presence of a mirror world.
we have proposed a particle physics model which could explain the non-observation at IceCube and predict the flavour ratios of observed neutrinos.

we propose a possible explanation of IceCube observations of non-detection of muon events in the context of a particle physics model which is testable in the future experiments like IceCube, T2K, NOvA, Hyper-Kamiokande, etc.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IceCube observation can be explained in terms of neutrinos oscillations and that the model can be tested in the near future by the next generation of neutrino telescopes.
the IceCube observation of the non-observance of muon neutrinos coincident with GRBs could be explained by the existence of a mirror world.
the non-observation at IceCube can be explained in terms of a new physics model that predicts new physics at the TeV scale.
